content: I have researched open-source JavaScript, React, and Remotion repositories for VideoScribe-style whiteboard animations where a hand PNG draws an SVG path. Here are the top 2 repositories that provide complete, out-of-the-box solutions, along with their mechanics and limitations: ### 1. NadirWeb-App/Inkplainer-OS **Overview:** A free, open-source whiteboard animation maker that runs entirely in the browser using pure JavaScript and HTML5. **How it works:** It acts as a full VideoScribe alternative GUI. It processes SVGs and text, animating them stroke-by-stroke. It includes a "Drawing Mode" that gives users control over hand behavior, direction, and stroke timing. Everything is processed locally via `IndexedDB` and it exports directly to MP4/WebM. **Limitations:** - It is a standalone GUI web app, not an importable React component or Remotion template that you can just `npm install`. - No backend support or programmable API; it relies on the user interacting with the browser GUI. ### 2. Vincentwei1021/anything2explainer **Overview:** An open-source tool and "agent skill" built on React and **Remotion**. It takes a topic and programmatically renders a motion-graphics explainer video. **How it works:** Instead of relying on generative AI video, it uses Remotion to programmatically draw every frame on a "black canvas," complete with vector line art, progress bars, and TTS voiceovers. It orchestrates the entire pipeline from storyboard to parallel rendering of shots. **Limitations:** - It's heavily opinionated (black canvas, specific typography) and built as an agent tool (for Claude Code/Codex) rather than a lightweight whiteboard animation library. - It uses a **PolyForm Noncommercial license**, meaning it cannot be used for commercial projects. ### How Developers Implement "The Hand Tracking" in React/Remotion While there isn't a single definitive, drop-in `@remotion/whiteboard` component library, developers typically build the effect themselves using these mechanics: 1. **React / Framer Motion:** They animate the SVG `pathLength` property using `framer-motion`. 2. **Remotion:** Using the `@remotion/paths` package, developers use the `getPointAtLength()` function. They animate the path's progress over time, drawing the partial stroke. They then pass the exact `(x, y)` coordinates returned by `getPointAtLength()` to an absolute-positioned ``, ensuring the hand strictly follows the tip of the line being drawn. (A notable mention is `ytrofr/claude-remotion-editor` which includes a "SceneDirector" to interactively record mouse/hand paths over Remotion compositions, and `Danilaa1/drawably` which generates "boiling" hand-drawn UI sketch lines in React without the hand PNG).
